title: codegen: testcontainer-backed live smoke test for generated repositories
description:
Owner-flagged idea (2026-07-11): spin up a real neo4j v5-community via testcontainers-go and verify that the emitted repository code actually queries a live driver — not just type-checks against v5.28.4.

Scope suggestion (per C1 orchestrator brief):
- internal/codegen/live_test.go with build-tag codegen_live so CI stays opt-in.
- Testcontainer running neo4j:5-community.
- Steps:
  1. Generate a repo from a valid fixture (probably many_col_many for a decent surface).
  2. Compile the generated package into a small test binary.
  3. Seed the neo4j with a few known rows.
  4. Run the test binary against the live db.
  5. Assert :one and :many methods return the expected data (Row struct field values, ErrNoRows, ErrMultipleResults).

Rationale for deferring past C1:
- The goldens and just test-codegen-fence already prove the emitted code compiles + lints under the pinned driver — the type-check gap is closed.
- Adding testcontainers introduces a Docker dep and CI-time increase that changes the character of the internal/codegen test suite (pure Go today).
- The gap this closes is 'compiles + lints' vs 'actually queries' — real, but not blocking C1's DoD. Better to land it as its own PR cycle with the Docker-CI wiring done deliberately.

Priority: medium — worth doing before v1 GA so the emitted-code contract is battle-tested against a real driver.

Testcontainer-backed neo4j:5-community harness with codegen_live build tag; verifies emitted repo code queries a live driver. GH #227 auto-closed via 'Closes #227' in PR body. title: Model unfreeze: CALL-arg attribution dropped on the wire — no argument-site type check possible
description: OWNER DECISION REQUIRED (ADR 0008 revision protocol; freeze-not-a-wall policy). The frozen wire model discards CALL argument attribution entirely: internal/query/cypher/call.go:54-66 mines each argument expression's type then DISCARDS it (explicit bucket-3 comment), emitting parameter uses as untagged ExprUse{t, ExprInProjection} and argument refs as bare names into curPart.refs. query.CallBinding (query.go:843-910) carries no arg-type/arg-ref/CallArg fields. The Stage-14 parser spec §4.5 (docs/specs/cypher-query-parser-stage-14.md:971-990) skiplists the arg-vs-param type check as bucket-3 by design. Consequence: ADR 0009's R7 line 'argument assignability including NUMBER assignable-from INTEGER-or-FLOAT (ADR 0007 Stage-14 note)' has NO application site in the resolver — R7 shipped YIELD typing + gate lift + parser-authoritative unknown-procedure only, with the delta documented in docs/specs/resolver-stage-r7.md §7.1.1. Proposed widening: per-position CALL-arg records on CallBinding (arg query.Type + param name/token from the matched procsig.Signature) emitted at parse; the resolver's argument-site check incl. NUMBER assignable-from INTEGER-or-FLOAT then becomes a subset/assignability walk over those records. Same attribution family as gqlc-fvo (Use→Part) — consider deciding both together.
close_reason: Delivered across PRs #121 (spec), #122 (model unfreeze: CallBinding.args axis, ADR 0008 amendment), #123 (resolver argument-site assignability walk incl. NUMBER assignable-from + TypeNull wildcard, sentinel ErrCallArgAssignability, 4 new fixtures), #125 (spec errata: fabricated witnesses corrected, census pinned, TypeNull E1), #124 (R7 §7.1.1 closed-out errata). title: Model unfreeze: Use→Part attribution — parameter Uses carry no Part field

Consequence: the resolver cannot attribute a parameter PropertyUse to the Part it lexically occurs in, so R5 ships the any-valid-witness rule (resolve.go witnessAcrossScopes: witness in EVERY scope containing the Ref's variable, keep successes, unify via R2 lattice, error only when all containing scopes fail with ErrUnknownProperty). Proposed: add Part index (or Part ref) to the Use records at emission. Would let the resolver witness exactly in the lexical scope and delete the any-valid-witness workaround.

title: schema/gql: length/precision/scale field on PropertyType — an ADR 0002 reversal, blocked on a named consumer
description:
Split out of gqlc-h9n.16 (Problem B) after a design pass measured the blast radius. gqlc-h9n.16 keeps Problem A, the width fold.

STRING(10), CHAR(4), VARCHAR(5), DECIMAL(10,2) carry information the model has no constant for. Honouring them needs a new field on PropertyType.

## This is a reversal of a recorded decision, not a bug fix

docs/adr/0002-bit-width-preserving-value-type-model.md, verbatim: 'GQL type spellings are normalised into this enum (e.g. SMALLINT~Int16, ...); length and precision qualifiers (VARCHAR(255), DECIMAL(p,s)) are dropped.'

The tree also has a passing test named TestPropertyLengthQualifiersDropped (internal/schema/gql/propertytype_test.go:108) whose doc comment cites ADR 0002 and whose five rows are exactly VARCHAR(255), CHAR(8), STRING(100), DECIMAL(10, 2), FLOAT(10). Four of the five die under this bead. Deleting a test called ...QualifiersDropped is the honest signal that a decision is being reversed, and it should be reviewed as an ADR amendment rather than as a defect fix.

## Why it is blocked rather than merely deferred

Nothing would read the field. Measured: codegen.goType (internal/codegen/types.go:157) dispatches on PropertyType alone; CHAR(4) and bare CHAR both emit 'Amount string' and Go has no fixed-length string type to emit into. DECIMAL(10,2) and bare DECIMAL both die at ErrUnrepresentableWidth (internal/codegen/prepare.go:489) — precision and scale change nothing about there being no Go carrier. There is no plausible consumer without either a math/big DECIMAL carrier (declined in ADR 0002's Consequences, deferred to codegen) or a length-validating setter, which no bead proposes.

So the acceptance criterion is: name the consumer first.

## Cost when it does land — measured, and low

The designer ran the migration in a scratch worktree; patch kept at /tmp/h9n16/struct-experiment.patch. Changing 'type PropertyType string' to a struct with Base+Len, converting the const block to var, and adding String() plus MarshalJSON produced exactly TWO compile errors in the whole tree (internal/resolver/validated.go:123 and internal/codegen/prepare_test.go:306, both mechanical string(x) -> x.String()). After those, go build and the full go test suite are green with ZERO golden-file changes — MarshalJSON preserves the "type":"STRING" wire form.

One real cost: Go cannot const a struct, so 26 TypeXxx constants become mutable package-level vars. Mitigation if that matters: nest, with 'type BaseType string' keeping the const block and PropertyType wrapping it.

## The trap that must not be missed

unionProperty (internal/resolver/resolve.go:744) and unify (:844) compare property types with !=. If the length lands inside PropertyType, then CHAR(4) vs CHAR(8), STRING(5) vs STRING(10), and CHAR(4) vs bare CHAR all START FAILING — a large silent behaviour change across every union, WITH carry and UNION column, in exchange for a field codegen does not read. Either the length lives outside the compared value, or unionProperty/unify must compare base-only. The struct comparison will silently do the wrong thing by default, so this has to be decided explicitly.

## Ordering

gqlc-h9n.21 MUST land before this bead, in its own PR, green. h9n.21 asserts require.Equal(model(CHAR(4)), model(CHAR)), which is true today and false after this lands — so it goes red exactly when this bead closes the blind spot, which is the entire point of h9n.21. If this lands first, h9n.21 can never be written as specified and becomes dead work.

## Half-closure to be aware of

Even with a length field, CHAR(4) and VARCHAR(4) still resolve identically, because typeSpellings maps CHAR, VARCHAR and STRING all to graph.TypeString. Fixed-versus-variable is a SECOND dropped bit this bead does not recover. h9n.21's scalar_char_fixed_length case must therefore be paired against bare CHAR, as h9n.21 specifies; pairing it against VARCHAR(4) would never go red.

title: ci: nothing enforces the GOLANGCI_LINT_CACHE / ci.yml path coupling
description:
PR #396 made the golangci-lint cache per-worktree by changing two things that must agree:

- `justfile`: `export GOLANGCI_LINT_CACHE := justfile_directory() + "/.bin/golangci-cache"`
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: `actions/cache` `path: .bin/golangci-cache`

Nothing in the tree fails if a future edit drops or diverges either half.

## Why that is worse than a normal untested invariant

The failure is silent and has no error signal. Reviewer verified the
counterfactual against `ci.yml:36-43`: with `path:` back at
`~/.cache/golangci-lint` while the justfile still exports `.bin/golangci-cache`,
the restore step populates a directory `just lint` never reads, lint runs cold,
and the post-job save writes a stale cache under the `run_id`-unique primary key.
CI stays green. The only symptom is the lint job quietly costing ~78s instead of
~0.6s, forever, until someone notices the wall-time.

Divergence in the other direction reintroduces gqlc-6rv itself.

## Possible shape

A CI step or just recipe that asserts `.bin/golangci-cache` is non-empty after
`just lint`. Cheap (sub-second) and it fails loudly at the point of divergence.
Per the house preference for just recipes over inline workflow steps, this
probably belongs in the justfile with CI invoking it.

Not obviously worth its own PR — good candidate to fold into the next CI change.

Source: rev-6rv review of PR #396, nit N2 (non-blocking). Measured costs in that
review: cold 78.4s, warm 0.6s, 20 MiB per warm worktree.

title: schema/gql: four corpusAreas prefixes match no file — fill or drop
description:
`corpusAreas` (`internal/schema/gql/corpus_test.go:148`) declares 13 path prefixes
across the five areas. Four of them match no corpus file at `7217b18`:

| prefix | area | files |
|---|---|---|
| `18.5-property-types/` | B | 0 |
| `18.6-property-type/` | B | 0 |
| `18.7-property-value-type/` | B | 0 |
| `18.10-field-type/` | D2 | 0 |

The other nine carry all 86 files. The four directories do not exist on disk.

A prefix that matches nothing is inert — `requireOwnedByArea` only ever consults
prefixes to *admit* a file — so this is not a live fault. It is a claim the tree
makes and does not keep, and `corpusArea`'s own doc comment says prefixes are "the
only place a clause directory is named, so a typo in an entry's path fails instead
of quietly creating a directory". An unbacked prefix weakens exactly that.

## The choice, and why it is not cosmetic

The clause-18.5 / 18.6 / 18.7 / 18.10 productions **are** covered — the gate reads
`rules 133/133`. They are covered by files filed under *other* clause directories:
any node with a property reaches `propertyTypes` / `propertyType` /
`propertyValueType`, and record types reach `fieldType`. So the empty prefixes are
a symptom of the incidental-carrier class, not a separate problem — the names are
green, but no file whose *subject* is those clauses reaches them.

That argues for filling rather than deleting: four small files, one per clause,
whose header comment says what production they are the deliberate carrier of.
Deleting the prefixes is the cheaper option and is defensible if the view is that
these productions have no surface syntax of their own worth a dedicated file —
but that should be an explicit decision recorded in the comment, not a silent
tidy-up.

Decide one way or the other; do not leave four prefixes asserting a partition that
does not exist.

Related: the incidental-carrier gating bead — if that detector lands and is
prefix-driven, these four empty prefixes will need a disposition anyway.

Discovered while reviewing PR #392.

title: schema/gql: promote parse-shape recording from report to gate
description:
The alternative-level obligation set landed in gqlc-h9n.2 counts *labelled alternatives* (`rule#N`). linus established during that bead that this undercounts the real branching surface, and team-lead ruled the wider measure lands as a **report** rather than a gate so that five parallel corpus authors were not re-briefed mid-flight (amendment A10).

Measured surface, 2026-07-25: **319 branch points** — 174 top-level alternatives, 8 nested-group, 137 optionality. Of the 137 optionality points, **129 have neither branch demanded** by any obligation.

Worked example of why `rule#N` cannot see it: `NODE TYPE LABEL A` and `NODE LABEL A` produce the **identical** `nodeTypePhraseFiller` shape `[nodeTypeFiller]`, because the spelling difference turns on `TYPE?` in the *parent* rule. So that distinction is invisible to alternative-counting *and* to per-rule shape recording of `nodeTypePhraseFiller` itself. Any promotion has to record shapes in a way that attributes a parent-rule optionality point to the place an author can act on.

What exists after gqlc-h9n.2: distinct ordered-child shapes are accumulated per rule and the totals are logged. There is deliberately no pinned count and no checked-in golden — a golden that moves whenever any author adds a corpus file is a merge-conflict generator, so the artifact is written only behind an opt-in flag.

This bead decides whether the 319 is an obligation, and if so how much of it. It is not a foregone conclusion: a large fraction of the 129 may be uninteresting optionality (whitespace-equivalent keyword elision) rather than distinct semantics, and gating on all of it would be the uncloseable-gate mistake that A1§3 and A9 both had to correct. Read the number first, partition it, then gate on the part that is worth files.
acceptance_criteria:
The 319 branch points are partitioned into semantically distinct spellings versus uninteresting optionality, with the criterion written down rather than judged case by case.
A decision is recorded on whether the distinct partition becomes a gate, with reasoning, including the option of not gating.
If gated: the golden artifact is generated once and the gate is fail-closed, so a scanner regression yielding an empty shape set cannot pass.
Parent-rule optionality points are attributed to a rule an author can act on, not to the rule whose shape is unchanged by them.

title: docs: correct the GQL.g4 provenance claim — community ANTLR adaptation, not a WG3 artifact
description:
`internal/grammar/gql/GQL.g4` is described in beads, code comments and triage
notes as "a faithful ISO GQL grammar". That overstates its provenance.

Established 2026-07-25: the file is **byte-identical** to
`antlr/grammars-v4/gql/GQL.g4` — a community-contributed grammar (author "Miotto
Nicola"), not a WG3 or standards-editor artifact. Visible ANTLR adaptations and
transcription artifacts:

- `procedureSpecification` alternatives commented out
- `connectorUndirected : TO | TILDE` overlapping `connectorPointingRight : TO |
  RIGHT_ARROW`, an ambiguity ISO resolves with syntax rules (see gqlc-h9n.9 item 4)
- a misplaced `// 19.9 <labled predicate>` section comment (also misspelled)

Its graph-type DDL section does match, rule-for-rule, TuGraph's independently
maintained ISO GQL grammar — which is real corroboration, and worth stating
*instead* of the faithfulness claim.

## Why this is worth a bead rather than a silent edit

The claim shaped a wrong conclusion during triage. "The grammar is faithful and
is not the problem" was used to move attention to the listener, which happened to
be correct that time. But the same reasoning would have suppressed investigation
of a genuine grammar defect, and two candidates already exist: the `TO` ambiguity
above, and the fact that a full check of all 3774 lines against Annex A was not
possible because the standard is paywalled.

## Deliverable

Replace the faithfulness claim wherever it appears with an accurate provenance
note: upstream source, the fact that it is a community adaptation, what was
verified (graph-type DDL vs TuGraph, rule-for-rule) and what was not (the other
~3700 lines, unverifiable against a paywalled Annex A). Anywhere the grammar is
treated as authoritative for a semantic question, say that it cannot answer prose
questions — the endpoint-alias investigation in gqlc-uhb is the worked example.
acceptance_criteria:
Every 'faithful ISO GQL grammar' claim is replaced with an accurate provenance note naming the upstream antlr/grammars-v4 source and its community authorship.
The note states what was verified (graph-type DDL matches TuGraph's independent grammar rule-for-rule) and what was not (the remaining lines, unverifiable against a paywalled Annex A).
The known ANTLR adaptations and transcription artifacts are listed.
Anywhere the grammar is used to settle a semantic question, a note records that it cannot answer prose questions.

title: schema/gql: four undefined-or-unrecorded graph-type DDL behaviours
description:
Four small graph-type DDL behaviours that are individually not worth a bead but
collectively leave the accepted subset undefined. Each needs a decision and a
test, most of them one line.

## 1. A node type with properties but no labels is rejected

    nodeTypeImpliedContent : nodeTypeLabelSet | nodeTypePropertyTypes | nodeTypeLabelSet nodeTypePropertyTypes    # GQL.g4:1528-1532

The middle alternative is properties with no label set. Verified 2026-07-25:
`NODE TYPE P (p {id STRING})` fails with `ErrUnnamedNodeType` ("node type has no
label"). Grammar-legal, so decide: is an unlabelled node type meaningful for a
generator that names Go types after labels? Probably not — but say so, and make
the error explain *that*, rather than implying the author forgot something.

## 2. A qualified graph type name keeps only its last component

`EnterCreateGraphTypeStatement` (listener.go:92) reads
`c.CatalogGraphTypeParentAndName().GraphTypeName().Identifier().GetText()` and
discards the parent path, so `CREATE GRAPH TYPE /a/b/G AS { ... }` resolves as if
it were `G` (verified 2026-07-25).

This one is **already decided and already pinned** — `TestGraphTypeName`
(parser_test.go:71-90) has a "catalog path keeps last component" case, and the
docstring explains the reasoning. So it is not a silent reinterpretation and needs
no code change.

What it needs is a line in the ADR, and a note that it becomes load-bearing if
`COPY OF` is ever supported (gqlc-h9n.1), since that form references a graph type
*by catalog path* — at which point discarding the parent stops being harmless.
Listed here only so the ADR does not omit it.

## 3. IF NOT EXISTS and OR REPLACE parse and are ignored

Both are in `createGraphTypeStatement` (GQL.g4:344). Ignoring them is correct for
a static generator with no catalog to check against or replace in — there is only
ever one graph type and it is always "created".

Like item 2 this is **already pinned** by `TestGraphTypeName` (parser_test.go:79-80,
the "or replace ignored" and "if not exists ignored" cases), so no code or test
change is needed. It needs one ADR line each so a future reader does not mistake
the silence for an oversight.

## 4. `(a TO b)` is grammatically ambiguous and resolved only by rule order

    connectorPointingRight : TO | RIGHT_ARROW     # GQL.g4:1659-1662
    connectorUndirected    : TO | TILDE           # GQL.g4:1664-1667

`TO` appears in both, and `endpointPair : endpointPairDirected |
endpointPairUndirected` lists directed first, so ANTLR resolves `CONNECTING
(a TO b)` as pointing-right. That is almost certainly the intended reading — ISO
disambiguates with syntax rules that an ANTLR grammar cannot express — but gqlc
depends on ANTLR's first-alternative-wins behaviour for it.

This matters directly to the phrase-form work (gqlc-uhb): if `TO` ever resolved
as undirected, every `CONNECTING (X TO Y)` would hit the undirected rejection.
Pin it with a test so a future grammar regeneration or rule reordering cannot
flip it silently.
acceptance_criteria:
A node type with properties and no labels has a decided outcome and an error that explains the reason rather than implying an omission.
A test pins CONNECTING (a TO b) as pointing-right, so the connector ambiguity cannot flip silently on grammar regeneration.
UNDIRECTED ... CONNECTING (a TO b) has a golden pinning today's directed-endpoint-pair misparse, as the phrase-form twin of the gqlc-h9n.3 arc-form case.
The already-pinned behaviours (qualified name truncation, IF NOT EXISTS, OR REPLACE) each get an ADR line; no code change is made to them.
The ADR notes that qualified-name truncation becomes load-bearing if COPY OF is ever supported.

comments.author: areqag
comments.text:
This bead is why the gqlc-h9n.2 flagged-alternative criterion had to be rewritten, and it is worth recording because the near-miss was invisible.

connectorPointingRight : TO | RIGHT_ARROW  and  connectorUndirected : TO | TILDE both accept a bare TO, so which one wins is decided by ANTLR alternative order today. The original coverage criterion flagged an alternative only when its symbols were a subset of its SIBLINGS' symbols — and TO is unique among each rule's siblings, so neither TO alternative was flagged. But TO is also a temporal duration qualifier: '{ (:A { p :: DURATION(YEAR TO MONTH) }) }' covers the TO token while entering connectorPointingRight and connectorUndirected zero times, and 'CONNECTING (a -> b)' / 'CONNECTING (a ~ b)' enter both rules without either taking its TO alternative.

So the coverage gate would have gone fully green without ever compelling the file that exposes this bead. Verified on real parses by linus, reproduced independently by team-lead (/tmp/lead-invisible.py).

The criterion is now forbid-and-recompute: delete an alternative, rebuild the closure, and flag it if all 133 rules and 133 tokens are still reached. Under that criterion connectorPointingRight#1 and connectorUndirected#1 are both flagged, so the corpus is REQUIRED to contain all four connector spellings — bare TO for each rule plus -> and ~. Area C owns them.

DONE for this bead means the resolution no longer depends on ANTLR ordering, with those four files distinguishing the two rules.

comments.author: areqag
comments.text:
Item 4 is sharper and worse than written. Verified 2026-07-25 (team-lead, /tmp/h9n2probe/leadconn), two corrections:

1. It is not just 'resolved by rule order' — edgeKind is never consulted at all. Prediction for endpointPair sees only the parenthesised token run, because endpointPairPhrase is a sibling of edgeTypePhraseFiller under edgeTypePhrase. So the DIRECTED/UNDIRECTED keyword is INERT at this decision. Measured, under both SLL and full LL:

    UNDIRECTED ... CONNECTING (a TO b)
      -> endpointPair > endpointPairDirected > endpointPairPointingRight > connectorPointingRight(TO)
         AMBIG rule=endpointPair alts={1,2} exact=true

2. The bead says the pointing-right reading is 'almost certainly the intended reading'. That holds for DIRECTED. It does NOT hold for UNDIRECTED: an undirected edge type whose endpoints are written (a TO b) gets a DIRECTED endpoint pair in the tree. That is a class-2 silent reinterpretation — the phrase-form twin of the arc-form case already tracked as gqlc-h9n.3 — and the phrase form is the spelling a human is more likely to write. It needs a golden pinning today's wrong output, not just a test pinning pointing-right on the directed case.

Consequence for gqlc-h9n.2: connectorUndirected#1 is UNREACHABLE, not merely invisible. No corpus file can take it, so it is exempt from the alternative obligation rather than demanded (amendment A9). If this bead ever makes edgeKind load-bearing for prediction, that exemption must be deleted and the alternative covered — the harness asserts the exemption bidirectionally, so it will go red on its own and tell you.

title: schema/gql: ADR the rejected value-type families — PATH, RECORD, dynamic unions, references, immaterial
description:
Six value-type families in GQL.g4 §18.9 that a static code generator targeting
property-graph storage plausibly *should* refuse — but which today share the
single generic `ErrUnsupportedType` sentinel and have no ADR recording the
reasoning.

    pathValueType    : PATH notNull?                                        # 1964
    recordType       : ANY? RECORD notNull? | RECORD? fieldTypesSpecification notNull?   # 1977-1980
    ANY VALUE? notNull?                                                     # 1728  open dynamic union
    ANY? PROPERTY VALUE notNull?                                            # 1729  dynamic property value
    ANY VALUE? <A|B>  /  A | B                                              # 1731-1732  closed dynamic union
    referenceValueType : graph | bindingTable | node | edge references      # 1900-1904
    immaterialValueType : nullType | emptyType   (NULL, NULL NOT NULL, NOTHING)  # 1907-1919

## Why this is a decision bead, not a feature bead

Several of these are not property value types in any storable sense. `PATH`, the
reference value types and the binding-table type describe *query result* values,
not stored properties — a node property cannot hold a path. `NOTHING` and `NULL
NOT NULL` are the empty type, inhabited by nothing, which cannot be a property
type at all. Under the no-dialect principle, refusing them is legitimate; what
is missing is the written reason.

`ANY PROPERTY VALUE` and the closed dynamic unions are the genuinely arguable
ones: they *are* property value types by construction, and a generator could map
them to `any` or to a generated sum type. Whether that produces code worth
having is the real question.

`RECORD` sits between the two — it is a structured value type, and
`fieldTypesSpecification` (1982) has its own `fieldType` rule (1996), so the
grammar fully describes it, but neo4j has no native record-valued property.

## Deliverable

An ADR per group, or one ADR with a section per group, each stating the concrete
reason for rejection — and, where the reason is "not representable in the
targeted store" rather than "not a property type", saying which store and why,
so the decision can be revisited when a different backend is targeted.

Replace the single generic `ErrUnsupportedType` for these with errors precise
enough that a schema author knows whether they hit a permanent boundary or an
unimplemented feature. That distinction is invisible today.
acceptance_criteria:
An ADR records a concrete reason for each rejected value-type family, distinguishing 'not a property value type' from 'not representable in the targeted store'.
The generic ErrUnsupportedType is replaced for these families by errors that say whether the boundary is permanent or unimplemented.
Each family has a test pinning its rejection to the specific error.

title: ci: cancel sibling jobs when any required blocking check fails
description:
Right now if one required blocking check in ci.yml fails (e.g. actionlint hits a transient network error on setup-just), the other required checks (lint/test/tidy/govulncheck/codegen-fence/live-smoke) all continue to completion. Wastes CI minutes and delays the failure signal on the PR. Especially painful on flaky network failures where a rerun of just the failed check would suffice.

Options to explore:
1. **Dependency chain**: put fast checks first (actionlint, tidy) as `needs:` for the slower ones (test, live-smoke). Slow jobs skip when fast fails. Simple, no third-party actions.
2. **Gate job pattern**: one lightweight 'gate' job that runs all fast validators; each expensive job `needs: [gate]`. Cleaner structure but changes the check-name topology (may affect required-status-checks ruleset).
3. **Runtime cancellation via API**: use `gh api` in a step to cancel sibling in-progress jobs on failure. More complex and racy.
4. **Concurrency groups per (workflow, PR)**: cancels prior runs on new pushes to same PR, but does NOT cancel sibling jobs within the same run.

Prefer option 1 for simplicity. Requires updating the ruleset's required_status_checks list if job names change.

Discovered 2026-07-19 during gqlc-23e recovery: PR #343 had one flaky actionlint failure while everything else passed; had to rerun just the failed job. If checks were chained, we'd have re-run only actionlint and skipped the passed ones automatically.

title: workflow: concurrent-session cwd coordination for shared repo
description:
Multiple agent sessions can operate on the same repo cwd (\`/home/antranig/Developer/gqlc/gqlc\`) simultaneously, running on different branches. Observed 2026-07-18 during gqlc-71n:

1. Session A on \`chore/gqlc-23e-release-pipeline-impl\` making bd metadata edits.
2. Session B (mine) working on gqlc-71n. Carmack on arrival found the tree checked out on session A's branch, not their own. Correctly switched.
3. Session A's staged \`.beads/issues.jsonl\` change persisted through the switch — no visible conflict, but a coordination hazard.
4. Later carmack switched back to their branch to complete work; sometime after Session A checked out its branch again, potentially with different HEAD.

Problems:
- No signaling between sessions about "I'm here, don't switch branches".
- Session A's staged changes travelled to session B's branch until carmack noticed.
- Team-lead reviews (running \`git status\`, \`git log\`) may inspect the wrong branch's state if branch drifts under them.

Mitigation used this session: sibling git worktree via \`git worktree add ../gqlc-71n-review <branch>\`. Kept my review isolated from session A's cwd state.

Longer-term options:
1. Institutionalize \`git worktree add\` per session (each session takes its own sibling worktree at spawn).
2. Session leader checks \`git branch --show-current\` before every branch-modifying op; if unexpected, use a worktree.
3. Documentation-level guidance in CLAUDE.md's session-completion checklist.

Filed for policy conversation. Non-blocking.
close_reason: Policy stated by user 2026-07-18: every modification-intent session runs in its own sibling worktree; shared repo cwd is read-only research only. No open policy question remaining. Documentation half being shipped via a small CLAUDE.md addition PR (this session); enforcement half is session discipline + memory (workflow-sibling-worktree-per-session).

title: release: add Homebrew tap (areqag/homebrew-gqlc) once release pipeline is stable
description:
Follow-up to [[gqlc-23e]] release automation. Once the tagpr + GoReleaser pipeline is proven stable (a few clean release cycles), enable first-class Homebrew distribution for the gqlc CLI.

Steps:
1. Create empty companion repo areqag/homebrew-gqlc (Homebrew tap convention: repo name must start with "homebrew-").
2. Uncomment the `brews:` block in .goreleaser.yaml (added as commented placeholder in gqlc-23e implementation, referencing this bead).
3. Create a fine-grained GitHub PAT with contents:write on areqag/homebrew-gqlc.
4. Add the PAT as GH repo secret HOMEBREW_TAP_GITHUB_TOKEN in areqag/gqlc.
5. Cut a test release and verify formula lands in the tap repo.
6. Document `brew tap areqag/gqlc && brew install gqlc` in README.

Not urgent: `go install github.com/areqag/gqlc/cmd/gqlc@latest` covers Homebrew's audience today. Deferred while the CLI is 0.0.x experimental — no point building distribution ergonomics until the surface is stable enough that users would actually pin a version.

title: chore(hooks): reject Co-Authored-By claude trailers + CLAUDE.md AI-attribution rule
description:
Hard-enforce the "no AI attribution in commits/PRs" style rule (see
[[feedback-no-ai-attribution-in-prs-or-commits]]) via three layers, of
which two require code changes:

1. **Local commit-msg hook** (\`.githooks/commit-msg\`) — reject any
   commit whose message contains a Co-Authored-By trailer matching
   Claude/Anthropic patterns (case-insensitive on the trailer key;
   match \`claude\` in the value OR \`@anthropic\.com\` in the email).
   Exit non-zero with a helpful message pointing at the CLAUDE.md
   section. Silent success on clean commits. Same wiring as other
   \`.githooks/*\`: activated by \`core.hooksPath=.githooks\` (already
   set via \`just init\`).

2. **CLAUDE.md AI-attribution section** — document the rule, its
   rationale (AI use is a given; explicit disclosure is noise; bot
   contributor pollutes GH authorship signal), and reference the
   commit-msg hook enforcement.

3. **PR-body footer** (the \`🤖 Generated with Claude Code\` line) —
   deliberately NOT hook-enforceable because PR bodies bypass local
   git. Rely on the CLAUDE.md rule + memory for this half. Escalate
   to a CI check on PR body if it recurs.

Also add tests: a \`.githooks/tests/commit-msg-test.sh\` in the same
shape as the existing \`.githooks/tests/claude-pre-bash-test.sh\`,
wired into \`just test-hooks\`. Should cover: rejects mixed-case
trailer keys, rejects claude in value, rejects anthropic.com email,
accepts clean commit, accepts human co-author.

Impact: the only commit in the recent session that surfaced Claude
as a GH contributor was fdddba39 (chore beads close-out) via its
\`Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\`
trailer. With this hook in place, that commit would have been
rejected at commit time.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #330. Three-layer enforcement: (1) .githooks/commit-msg rejects Co-Authored-By trailers matching claude/anthropic patterns, skipping merge commits via MERGE_HEAD; (2) .githooks/tests/commit-msg-test.sh covers 7 cases wired into just test-hooks; (3) CLAUDE.md 'AI attribution' section documents the rule and hook-enforcement scope. Live-hook meta-check confirmed core.hooksPath wiring. From next commit forward, no Co-Authored-By: Claude trailers can land.

title: codegen-live: promote nightly to PR-blocking merge gate
description:
Promote .github/workflows/codegen-live.yml from workflow_dispatch +
nightly cron to a PR-blocking check on the merge gate. The codegen ->
driver contract is currently only exercised against a real neo4j once
a day; a regression that ships in a codegen refactor sits on master
for up to 24h before nightly surfaces it. Blocking on PR closes that
window.

Precondition: gqlc-9u5 (Go test cache enabled) must be merged first.
Without cache, this promotion imposes ~30s on every PR — violates the
ci-speed-parity invariant. With cache, a typical PR pays <1s
(cached PASS); only PRs that touch codegen-relevant paths pay ~30s.

Changes:
1. Add on.pull_request to codegen-live.yml (already has push:master +
   nightly cron; add pull_request).
2. Update the workflow docstring to reflect its new role — no longer
   an opt-in satellite, now a merge-gate.
3. Consider a paths: filter (belt + suspenders alongside Go's cache).
   Path candidates: internal/codegen/**, internal/resolver/**,
   internal/schema/**, internal/queryfile/**, test/data/codegen/**,
   .github/workflows/codegen-live.yml, justfile. Miss one and we'd
   falsely skip; skip if the cache is trusted enough.

Depends on: gqlc-9u5.
Descends from: gqlc-5gc scope discussion.
close_reason: Code half shipped in PR #323 (on.pull_request trigger). Config half shipped via gh api PATCH (gqlc-oe0) — required_status_checks.contexts now includes live-smoke. Promotion fully enforced.

title: codegen-live: enable Go test cache in CI
description:
Wire the codegen-live workflow so Go's test cache actually works across
CI runs. Today \`just test-codegen-live\` (justfile:98) passes \`-count=1\`,
the canonical opt-out from Go's test result cache. Combined with
actions/setup-go@v5 defaulting cache-dependency-path to root go.sum
(missing the nested test/data/codegen/go.sum), we get zero cache hits
on the live-smoke workflow even when nothing that could affect the
generated code has changed.

Changes:
1. Remove \`-count=1\` from the test-codegen-live recipe. Go's cache
   invalidates automatically when any input file (source, test binary,
   env vars the test reads via os.Getenv) changes.
2. Add cache-dependency-path: |\n     go.sum\n     test/data/codegen/go.sum
   to actions/setup-go@v5 in .github/workflows/codegen-live.yml so
   nested-module dep bumps invalidate the cache correctly.
3. Pin neo4jImage in test/data/codegen/live_test.go from
   "neo4j:5-community" to a digest ("neo4j@sha256:..."). Mutable tags
   would allow neo4j to push a rebuild under the same string, and Go's
   cache — which trusts the string constant as the input — would serve
   a stale PASS. Digests are immutable, so any digest bump naturally
   invalidates the cache.

Result: cache-miss = full ~30s run (v5 + v6 arms in parallel).
Cache-hit = <1s "(cached)" without touching docker. Sets up the
follow-up bead promoting the workflow to PR-blocking.

Precedes: codegen-live PR-blocking promotion bead.
Descends from: gqlc-5gc scope discussion.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #322. Removed -count=1 from just test-codegen-live, added cache-dependency-path with both root + nested go.sum, pinned neo4jImage to multi-arch manifest-list digest sha256:362542416.... Cache now serves (cached) PASS on unchanged inputs; sets up gqlc-rvw's PR-blocking promotion.

title: codegen: investigate SingleT/CollectT shape for :one and :many emission
description:
Explore whether the generated :one and :many methods should route through
neo4j.SingleT[T]/CollectT[T] instead of the current \`records, err := q.db.run(...)\`
+ manual \`len(records)\` sentinel-branching shape (see generated
test/data/codegen/valid/*/golden/queries.cypher.go and db.go).

Trade-offs to evaluate:
  * Less emitted boilerplate per :one method
  * SingleT folds "zero rows" and "multiple rows" into one error — losing
    the current ErrNoRows / ErrMultipleResults sentinel granularity that
    is the semantic contract of :one. Any shape change must preserve
    (or deliberately drop, with owner sign-off) that contract.
  * :many currently materialises \`[]*neo4j.Record\` then decodes; a
    CollectT[T]-based path could inline the mapper.
  * Interacts with gqlc-1a5 (:iter streaming cardinality, post-v1).

Deferred from the gqlc-5gc scope discussion: verified v5 and v6 both
expose SingleT/CollectT, so this is a codegen-quality question, not a
driver-version question. Do the investigation before committing to a
shape.

title: cypher parser tests: rebaseline cost of the ~112 surviving authored mustParse pins (post-ls8.5 residual)
description: gqlc-ls8.5's mechanical census showed only 43 of 159 hand-built mustParse pins are shape-mirrors of existing goldens; ~112 are authored inputs the mustParse doctrine (parser_test.go preamble) and TestGoldenOrphans rightly forbid converting to goldens (evidentiary circularity: round-tripping launders current parser behavior into 'expected', and -update silently rebases thereafter). So the original 'maintenance outlier' complaint — every additive model axis costs manual edits across parser_test.go — is only PARTIALLY closed by ls8.5; the authored pins retain that cost. This bead evaluates what, if anything, reduces it without weakening evidence: candidates include (a) contributing authored scenarios upstream to the TCK corpus so they earn goldens legitimately, (b) helper/table consolidation so additive zero-valued axes are absorbed without per-case edits, (c) a narrowly-safeguarded doctrine amendment (would need a first-golden review protocol that answers the silent -update objection concretely). Deliberately open-ended; a 'no action, cost is the price of evidence' close is acceptable if analysis supports it.

comments.author: antranig-yeretzian
comments.text:
gqlc-ls8.5 §9 Q3 by-stage consolidation detail (queued at Phase-3 close;
released post-verdict per team-lead ratification of PR #308 at f33296a).

Recording the concrete shape of candidate (b) — helper/table consolidation —
as it surfaced during the ls8.5 Phase-1/2/3 grill so the option is
actionable when this bead moves. Not a proposal; a factual snapshot of the
residual pin population by stage, which the ls8.5 census incidentally
produced.

By-stage rebaseline surface (from the residual 117 mustParse entries at
Phase-3 tip 3,528, per §2 outturn table):

- Stage 4 (UNION-nesting): every mustParse pin that exercises multi-branch
  structure carries the same one-branch-per-part scaffolding through
  `oneBranch` / `oneWriteBranch`. An additive Stage-4 axis change (e.g. a
  new BranchState carrier field) forces per-pin manual edits across every
  authored UNION-nested pin. Contiguous rebaseline section: group these
  pins into a Stage-4 subsection of the mustParse map so an axis-change
  touches N helper-lines instead of N-pins.

- Stage 12 (write-side statements): every pin using `oneWriteBranch`
  asserts on the StatementKind axis end-to-end. An additive write-side
  axis (statement-scope, per-clause write metadata, etc.) forces the same
  pattern of per-pin manual edits. Contiguous rebaseline section: group
  Stage-12 write pins together so the helper carries the axis burden.

- Stage 14 (CALL / procsig-carrying pins): the residual sig-divergent
  keeper + any future Class-A sig-carrying pins whose sigs diverge from
  Background sigs. An additive procsig axis (new `procsig.Signature`
  field, per-CallBinding metadata) forces manual edits across every
  Stage-14 pin. Contiguous rebaseline section: group Stage-14 CALL pins
  together with a shared authored-sigs helper so the axis-change
  touches the helper, not per-pin bodies.

Rationale: the ~20.7 gross lines/pin cost observed in the ls8.5 Phase-2
sweep (871 lines across 42 deletions; see spec §2 actuals table) is
dominated by the helper-invocation lines, not the pin body itself. A
consolidation that lifts the axis-touching lines into shared helpers
converts per-pin manual edits into per-helper manual edits without
weakening the independent-evidence property (the hand-derived Query
shape stays hand-derived; only the constructor scaffolding is shared).

Constraint the consolidation must preserve: the reviewer diffing an
axis-rebaseline PR must still be able to read each pin's expected
shape independently — the helper cannot become so terse that the pin's
target shape is inferred rather than stated. A helper that returns a
pre-shaped Query is a step too far; a helper that takes the axis values
as parameters and returns the composed Query is the ceiling.

Cross-refs: cypher-golden-test-migration.md §6 (per-pin cost analysis),
§9 Q3 (the parent question this comment operationalises). PR #308 sha
f33296a shipped the ls8.5 residual figures this consolidation would
target.

comments.author: antranig-yeretzian
comments.text:
Analysis (autonomous, 2026-07-18):

Verified census. `parser_test.go` at HEAD is 3,528 lines; `mustParse` runs L125-2610 and holds **117 pins** (matches ls8.5 Q1 outturn: 43+4+112 pre-migration, then 42 Class-A shape-mirrors deleted; residual = 117). Helper concentration inside the map:

- `oneBranch(query.Part{...})` — 74 top-level uses (60 pre-Stage-12, 1 Stage-13 "MERGE inside EXISTS does not flip", 14 Stage-14).
- `oneWriteBranch(query.Part{...})` — 12 top-level uses (9 Stage-12 write pins, 3 Stage-13 MERGE-write pins).
- 30 inline `query.Query{Branches: []query.Branch{{Parts: []query.Part{...}}}}` builds + 1 `func() query.Query {...}()` composer, all pre-Stage-12. Of the 30, 3 are true UNION shape (multi-branch: "union two branches", "union param branch attribution", "union all two branches"), ~7 are true WITH-chain shape (multi-part in one branch: "optional group ids span parts without reset", "with chain whole entity", "with chain value projection", "unwind list of lists", "return order by param", "with distinct", "exists body param via with-where", "unwind of list-of-nodes reused as node match"), and ~20 are single-branch/single-Part pins written raw — mostly Stage-6/7 temporal-arithmetic pins ("return date constructor", "return duration between", the six duration/date arithmetic pins around L637-682) plus a few Parameter-carrying pins that predate `oneBranch`'s variadic Parameters signature. These 20 could migrate to `oneBranch` today with no design change.

Stage bucketing of the 117 by file-position: Stages 0-11 hold 90 pins (concentrated in Stage 6 rich-projection/temporal, Stage 8 pattern shapes, and Stage 11 EXISTS-body pins — 15+ EXISTS-body pins in the L1397-1938 range dominate this segment); Stage 12 write pins hold 9; Stage 13 MERGE holds 4; Stage 14 CALL holds 14. Sig-carrying pins total 12 (11 with populated `sigs`, the sole `sigDivergentKeepers` member the survival case). The 3-way clustering the beads comment names (Stage 4 UNION-nesting, Stage 12 write-side, Stage 14 CALL/procsig) is only partly correct: Stage-14 CALL is a real 14-pin cluster with uniform `oneBranch`+`sigs` scaffolding; Stage-12 write is a real 9-pin cluster on `oneWriteBranch`; but Stage-4 UNION-nesting is only 3 pins — the comment's framing of "every authored UNION-nested pin" over-counts by conflating "multi-Part WITH chains" (~7 pins) with UNION (3 pins).

Empirical axis-cost check against the shipped model-change specs, which is the load-bearing calibration the bead is missing: **ay9** flipped **3 mustParse pins** (spec §4.3, L84-91: "optional match simple", "optional match reuses prior binding", "count distinct" — 4 `NewNullable*` invocations become `*InGroup(..., 1)`); the other 149 Binding-constructor invocations in the file stayed verbatim under `require.Equal`. **hk0** flipped **1 pin** ("count in arithmetic"); the other 24 ExprProjection assertions stayed verbatim (Shape B's zero-valued `ContainsAggregate` is bit-identical). **0ig** touched **11 pins** carrying 15 CallBinding invocations, of which only those with ≥1 argument rebaseline (spec §4.3). **5xg** flipped **0 pins** — Go zero-value equality holds. Ledger: 3 / 1 / 11 / 0. The bead description's "every additive model axis costs manual edits across ~112 pins" is empirically wrong; the actual cost per shipped axis has been 0-11 pins, and each cluster was the exact subset whose src exercised the changed axis.

Candidate evaluation. **(a) Upstream to TCK.** The 112 Class-C pins are authored precisely because the TCK is silent on the sentinel taxonomy they encode: 5xg's required-bare-ref flag, fvo's Use-part attribution, ay9's per-clause OptionalGroup — none of these are surface Cypher semantics the openCypher project would accept as scenarios. A handful (some MERGE and CALL kill-probes) plausibly map to legitimate skeptical scenarios, but even a maximally-successful contribution cycle would land ~5-10 scenarios upstream over several TCK bumps, converting <10% of the Class-C set at best, on a multi-quarter cadence outside gqlc's control. Cost/removal ratio is poor.

**(b) Helper/table consolidation.** The relevant axis cost per shipped spec is 0-11 pins per axis, i.e. it is not concentrated across all Class-C pins — the axis touches only pins whose src exercises it. Under `require.Equal` a helper that hides an axis inside its scaffolding gives you nothing you don't already have from Go zero-value equality: hk0's 24 non-flipping ExprProjection pins pay ZERO edit cost today. What consolidation could buy: for the 14 Stage-14 CALL pins, a helper `oneCallBranch(part query.Part, sigs []procsig.Signature, params ...query.Parameter) query.Query` co-locates the `sigs` field with the branch so any procsig axis change edits the helper; for the 3 UNION pins, `twoBranchUnion(a query.Branch, b query.Branch, kind query.UnionKind, params ...query.Parameter)` closes the raw-Branches inlining. Both preserve the "reviewer reads each pin's expected shape independently" constraint IF the helper returns a composed `query.Query` from parameterized inputs, not a pre-shaped Query. The real gain is measured in per-cluster line counts, not per-axis edits — which is a code-hygiene win, not a maintenance-outlier fix.

**(c) Doctrine amendment.** The `-update` laundering objection is concrete: minting a golden from an authored src runs the parser once under `-update`, records that output as expected, and every subsequent `-update` silently rebaselines through the same parser. A first-golden review protocol would need to (1) prohibit `-update` from ever touching an authored-origin golden except through a two-reviewer human sign-off that inspects the diff against the model contract, and (2) tag each authored golden at mint time with the ADR/spec §-ref that ratified its shape. Both are hard to enforce in code — `-update` is one flag on `go test`, not a per-file gate. Any protocol short of a file-level `//go:build authored-golden` guard that fails `-update` unless overridden by an environment variable will drift under time pressure. The safeguard exists as an idea but doesn't answer the objection concretely — it just adds a review layer over the same silent-rebase mechanism.

Recommendation. **Adopt a narrow (b) targeted at Stage-14, with 20-pin `oneBranch` migration cleanup as a separable follow-on.** Not (a) — the upstream conversion rate is too low. Not (c) — the doctrine amendment does not answer the `-update` objection concretely enough to override the lead ruling that stands from ls8.5 §1.4/§8. Not "no action" — the Stage-14 CALL cluster is a genuine 14-pin uniform-scaffold surface where an axis addition would touch every pin; consolidation here is a real win, not a code-hygiene wash.

Concrete helper signatures for (b):

```go
// oneCallBranch composes a Stage-14 one-branch/one-part CALL pin: same
// shape as oneBranch, plus authored procedure sigs the parser needs for
// registry-backed CALL resolution. Every Stage-14 mustParse pin uses
// this so a procsig axis change touches the helper, not per-pin bodies.
func oneCallBranch(
    part query.Part,
    sigs []procsig.Signature,
    params ...query.Parameter,
) (query.Query, []procsig.Signature)
```

Returning both the Query and the `sigs` slice lets the pin body destructure into `want, sigs` at the call site — the pin still names its `sigs` in-place, but any future field addition on `procsig.Signature` (a per-CallBinding metadata axis, an authored-vs-Background provenance bit, etc.) edits `oneCallBranch` once. Applies to all 14 Stage-14 pins.

```go
// twoBranchUnion composes a Stage-4 two-branch UNION pin: two branches
// (each supplied as an already-built Branch), a single combinator, and
// query-level Parameters. Every UNION pin in mustParse uses this so a
// combinator or per-branch metadata axis touches the helper, not the pin.
func twoBranchUnion(
    a query.Branch,
    b query.Branch,
    kind query.UnionKind,
    params ...query.Parameter,
) query.Query
```

Applies to 3 pins ("union two branches", "union param branch attribution", "union all two branches").

The 20 raw-inlined single-branch/single-Part pins ("return date constructor" through "return duration between", plus the temporal/arithmetic follow-ons at L637-682, plus the parameter-carrying pins that predate `oneBranch`'s variadic signature) should be migrated to `oneBranch(query.Part{...}, params...)` in a separable stylistic PR — no design change, no axis cost, just eliminating one class of divergent scaffolding a future reviewer would trip over. Explicitly NOT part of this bead's decision; log it as a separate low-priority code-hygiene bead. Not scoping to Stage 12 either: `oneWriteBranch` already exists and every Stage-12 write pin uses it. Not adding a "WithChain" helper — the 7 multi-Part WITH-chain pins each have a unique Part composition (part 1's Returns are the WITH projection; part 2's Bindings are what the MATCH-after-WITH introduces; the shapes diverge structurally); a helper here would either return a pre-shaped Query (violates the reviewer-reads-pin-shape constraint) or take so many parameters it's less legible than the inline form.

Constraints for future work. A bad first attempt at (b) would introduce a helper that materializes the pin's target shape from an axis argument the pin never names — e.g. `stage14CallPin(name string) query.Query` that hard-codes each pin's expected Query by key. That launders the same evidentiary circularity the mustParse doctrine forbids (the "expected" shape is now hidden in Go code the reviewer must dereference to read). The doctrine cliff: any helper whose return value contains a Bindings/Returns/Effects slice the caller did not pass in is over the line — the helper must be a pure composer of caller-supplied parts. A second cliff to avoid: coupling `oneCallBranch` to `sigs` provenance (Background-equal vs authored-divergent) — the coupling belongs at pin declaration site (as the current `sigDivergentKeepers` allowlist encodes it), not inside the helper. Signal of a bad attempt: the helper signature grows past ~4 parameters, or the pin body loses the ability to be read as "this src produces this shape" without stepping into the helper.

The bead's original headline — "every additive axis costs manual edits across ~112 authored pins" — should be closed as OVERSTATED at ls8.5 close. The load-bearing 112 Class-C pins are cheap under `require.Equal` for every axis whose zero value coincides with the pre-axis shape; the actual per-axis cost has been 0-11 pins, and each of those was the exact subset whose src exercised the axis, which is the cost of evidence, not of scaffolding. (b) removes a real 14-pin surface at Stage 14 without weakening evidence; the residual across Stages 0-11 stays authored, per doctrine, and per the empirical 0-3 pin-touch cost the shipped model-change record proves.

Independent verification: 117-pin count reproduced (main-checkout grep against L125-2610); 74/12/30/1 helper decomposition inspected; agent-attributed axis-flip counts (ay9=3, hk0=1, 0ig=11, 5xg=0) NOT independently re-verified against each PR's diff — best-effort agent claim. Owner call: pick between narrow (b) at Stage-14, "no action pending a real axis demand", or defer to a specific follow-up bead for the 14-pin oneCallBranch cutover.

title: codegen: v6-only column types — Vector + UUID (schema→resolver→codegen)
description: neo4j-go-driver v6 adds dbtype.Vector (Bolt 6.0) and native UUID (Bolt 6.1, v6.2.0). Mapping these as gqlc column types requires the full pipeline: schema property types, graph.PropertyType, resolver ResolvedType, codegen type tables (gated on DriverV6 — reject or fall back under DriverV5). Deliberately out of scope for the v6-option stack: no vector/uuid anywhere in internal/graph or internal/schema today, so this is schema-layer design work first. Also evaluated and deferred: v6.2 object-mapping preview API (unstable, preview-labelled — do not codegen against it); session.Run one-shot retry ADR-038 (generated code uses ExecuteRead/ExecuteWrite closures, no win).
design:
Design research banked 2026-07-12 (verified against driver 6.x branch + Neo4j docs):

DRIVER SHAPES: dbtype.UUID = [16]byte (RFC 9562, ParseUUID/String/TextMarshaler). dbtype.Vector[T VectorElement], VectorElement = float64|float32|int8|int16|int32|int64. neo4j.PropertyValue constraint (graph.go:25-30) already includes UUID and ALL SIX Vector instantiations -> generated decode via neo4j.GetProperty/GetRecordValue works unchanged; no new decode machinery.

SCHEMA SPELLING: adopt Cypher 25 official syntax VECTOR<FLOAT32>(1024) (element + dimension; used in IS :: constraints, Neo4j 2025.10+, requires v6 drivers). UUID: no GQL-standard spelling exists; propose bare UUID keyword.

GRAMMAR DELTA (the hard part): GQL.g4 valueType/predefinedType has NEITHER — UUID needs a predefinedType alternative + keyword token; VECTOR needs a parameterized rule (angle-bracket element + parenthesized dimension). Regen = just build-grammar = docker + ANTLR 4.13.1.

PIPELINE MAP: spellings table internal/schema/gql/propertytype.go:53-108 (canonicalSpelling normalization); enum internal/graph/propertytype.go:9-39 — NB flat enum cannot carry Vector's element+dimension: main modeling decision is PropertyType growing structure (or parallel fields) — deserves grilling/ADR. Resolver: ResolvedProperty passes graph.PropertyType through (resolve.go:1300,1345) — no resolver enum change for property-sourced columns. Codegen v5-rejection precedent: goType ok=false -> ErrUnrepresentableWidth at prepare.go:410/498/560 + types.go:254; UUID/Vector under DriverV5 should mirror it with a new error (requires-driver-v6), which means threading driverTarget into the prepare phases (today target only reaches render).

STAGING: (1) UUID first — no parameterization: keyword + TypeUUID + goType v6 arm + v5 rejection + _v6 goldens. (2) Vector second — grammar param type + PropertyType shape change, grill the modeling with the user first. Dimension: store for future constraint emission; Go carrier ignores it (Vector.Elems is a plain slice).
notes: 2026-07-12: claim released — implementation blocked on this host: grammar regen needs docker (none) or java (none). Design fully banked in DESIGN field; UUID stage is mechanical once grammar tooling is available; Vector stage needs a PropertyType-shape grill with the user first.

title: Wire procsig.Load into codegen CLI as -procsig flag
description: Follow-up to gqlc-6rz. title: resolver: builtin scalar-function signature table (elementId → string)
description: ADR 0010 D3 resolved entity structs as schema-shaped only; driver identity is accessed via explicit projection: RETURN p, elementId(p) AS id. The resolver currently types function invocations as unknown, so the alias renders as 'any' in generated code. Add a small builtin scalar-function signature table to the resolver — elementId(node|edge) -> string is the motivating entry; the same mechanism serves other builtins (id(), count(), etc.) later. When it lands, the recommended identity pattern types as string with zero codegen changes. Not blocking any C-stage.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #248. Parser-side builtin scalar-function signature table wired into classifyFunction + typeAtom; motivating entry elementId(node|edge) -> string plus id(node|edge) -> int. Codegen fixture identity_element_id/ pins the ADR 0010 D3 identity pattern rendering Id string (was any).

title: Codegen: :iter streaming cardinality (ADR 0010 D8, post-v1)
description: Fourth cardinality :iter generating streaming methods — func (q *Queries) X(ctx, ...) iter.Seq2[Row, error] — per ADR 0010 D8. Rationale: avoid sqlc's structural weakness where []Row materialisation makes full-result loads easy and streaming unretrofittable; neo4j driver streams natively and range-over-func scopes session cleanup to loop exit (early break included). v1 reserves the space only: cardinality is an open enum, method shapes assume no materialisation. Open design questions to settle when picked up: author-declared :iter vs auto-generated XIter sibling for every :many; interplay with SKIP/LIMIT pagination params; requires Go >= 1.23 in the user's module.
notes:
Design opens transferred from ADR 0010 D8 (grill close-out, 2026-07-11): (1) :iter as author-declared cardinality vs an auto-generated XIter sibling for every :many; (2) interaction with SKIP/LIMIT pagination parameters (orthogonal — document both). v1 committed exactly two enablers: cardinality is an open enum (annotation grammar admits :iter without a break) and nothing in the D2 method shape assumes materialisation. Session-lifetime hazard owns the design: iter.Seq2 scopes cleanup to loop exit incl. early break.

Design opens resolved (grill, 2026-07-11): ADR 0010 §D8 amended in PR #250 with seven Resolved-grill markers. Summary:
- Author-declared :iter opt-in (auto-XIter siblings rejected)
- :iter read-only; ErrIterOnWrite sentinel rejects writes
- Cardinality×shape validation extends symmetrically
- Method naming inherits §D2 verbatim
- Retry envelope: pre-first-yield only (post-yield errors yielded to caller, no double-yield)
- SKIP/LIMIT orthogonal
- Testing: goldens + gqlc-73h live smoke extension
Universal :iter (kill :many) considered and tabled for later revisit.
Implementation trigger: gated on user demand or benchmarked need. Grill markers in ADR are the paved runway.

title: GH↔bd sync: bd→GH close/update propagation for already-mirrored beads
description:
The GH↔bd sync hooks (PR #201) cover three directions:
- Post-merge pull: GH → bd (creates, closes, comments) — works.
- Session-start pull: GH → bd — works.
- Pre-push push: bd → GH — but ONLY for beads without external_ref (i.e., NEW beads).

Uncovered: bd → GH status/comment updates on ALREADY-MIRRORED beads. When an agent runs 'bd close gqlc-abc' on a bead that already has a GH mirror, the pre-push hook's filter (external_ref == null) skips it, and the GH mirror stays open until the human closes it manually.

Root cause: the fast filter needed to avoid the ~30s cost of 'bd github sync --push-only' (which scans every bead against GH) doesn't cover updates on existing beads. Session memory kv.memory.bd-github-sync-quirks notes that even --push-only may not reliably propagate close status (bd bug).

Options to close the gap (design decision pending):
1. Accept it — treat GH as the canonical close-decision surface; agent closes on bd are recommendations, human closes on GH are authoritative. Requires human touch on every close.
2. Track dirty beads via a marker file that bd updates on close/update, and pre-push consumes and clears.
3. Wait for a bd feature that emits close-since-last-sync events (upstream bd change).
4. Fall back to 'bd github sync --push-only' (30s) only when a fast preflight detects a locally-closed bead that has an external_ref. Requires a per-bead updated_at vs GH-updated_at compare that bd currently only exposes via full sync.

No consumer is blocked; the workflow degrades gracefully (human sees stale-open GH issue, closes manually, next post-merge propagates the close back into bd).
close_reason: Shipped in PR #318 (squash 81e5bec). Extended .githooks/bd-gh-sync push path: bulk gh issue list --state open intersected with closed-bd beads bearing external_ref; each mismatch gets gh issue close with a comment derived from close_reason. Verified live on push: 13 stale mismatches accumulated since PR #201 all closed cleanly (GH open 26→13, matching real open-bead count). Silent, idempotent, non-fatal. All CI green (tidy/lint/test/actionlint/codegen-fence/govulncheck).

title: Model / resolver: edge-side non-bare OPTIONAL-edge re-reference witness (post-5xg residual)
description: Post-5xg residual, filed at unfreeze cycle 5 close-out. The 5xg widening (PR #134) closes same-Part Class B same-Part bare-pattern demotion for both NodeBinding and EdgeBinding. However, the parser's bare-predicate (bare == chain-head with empty chain) is grammatically unreachable for edge variables — every edge sits between two nodes in a chain link. Consequently, an OPTIONAL-introduced edge re-referenced by name in a required chain link (e.g. OPTIONAL MATCH (a)-[r:R]->(b) MATCH (c)-[r]->(d) RETURN r) has ReferencedInRequiredBarePattern()==false and stays nullable under both 5xg and ay9 (its group has no proven member; itself is the OPTIONAL binding, not a witness). Neither Class A nor Class B closes this case. Candidate closures: (1) widen the 5xg parser predicate to admit edges in required chain links (would set flag on r); (2) add a distinct axis (e.g. ReferencedInRequiredChain []ClauseRef or bool); (3) treat this as an ay9 refinement (a same-name required chain-edge witnesses the OPTIONAL edge's group). Design decision pending. This is a legitimate under-demotion (lattice-safe under R4 §4.2) with a small blast radius (only OPTIONAL edges re-referenced by name in required chains).

title: Resolver: cross-Part OPTIONAL-group carry via branchState (post-ay9 residual)
description: Post-ay9 residual, filed at unfreeze cycle 4 close-out. The ay9 widening (PR #129) closes same-Part Class A OPTIONAL-clause-sibling demotion via a group-closure fixed point in demoteNullableInPlace. Cross-Part carry across WITH is unchanged: the resolver-internal branchState.exportedNullableBinding (internal/resolver/resolve.go:357-361) is name to bool and does not carry OPTIONAL-group ids. A binding carried across WITH keeps its own Nullable bit but loses its ay9-widened group closure — the downstream Part's demoter cannot see the source Part's OPTIONAL-group membership, so a WITH-carried OPTIONAL binding subsequently proven demotes only itself, not its group-siblings from the source Part. Extend branchState to carry OPTIONAL-group ids alongside the nullable bit (resolver-internal — no model change; ADR 0008 unaffected). Detail in docs/specs/unfreeze-ay9-optional-group.md sections 2.5 and 7 (residual note). This is a normal resolver refinement, not a model unfreeze.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #253 (feat(resolver): cross-Part OPTIONAL-group carry via branchState). Extended branchState.exportedOptionalGroup (name → int) so WITH-carried OPTIONAL bindings preserve group-id membership across Part boundaries. Group closure in demoteNullableInPlace unions carried and local memberships. Resolver-internal, no model change, ADR 0008 unaffected. New fixture demote_cross_with_optional_group.cypher; existing golden demote_bare_reference_composes_with_group flipped from Class A under-demote to tight demote (bonus 5xg §8.4 fixture 4 boundary lift). Spec ay9 §2.5+§7 amended. Recovered from stalled agent by orchestrator; force-push --lease after gci fix.

title: Use.Branch axis: UNION cross-branch attribution residuals (post-fvo)
description: Follow-up from unfreeze cycle 2 (gqlc-fvo, PR #118). Use records carry Part but no BRANCH index; the frozen model cannot derive per-branch Use counts (WHERE-body Uses leave no footprint on Part.Bindings/Returns/Effects — fvo spec erratum 2, §7.2.2 countUsesInBranch unimplementable). Shipped recovery: position cursor with Part-index-drop boundary detection + witnessInBranch cross-branch fallback at the SAME Part index on ErrUnknownProperty. Two verified residuals (linus, PR #118 review; no corpus fixture triggers either): (a) same-Part UNION boundary ambiguity — a Use invalid in its true branch but valid in a sibling branch at the same Part is admitted via fallback (any-valid-witness survives in the cross-branch direction only); (b) UNION-later-Part spurious rejection — branch 0 with fewer Parts than the Use's Part index hits ErrOutOfR0Scope on the primary try and the fallback does NOT recover from non-ErrUnknownProperty errors, so a Use genuinely in branch 1 Part 1 is spuriously rejected. Fix: additive 'branch int' axis on Use records under ADR 0008 revision protocol (or equivalent attribution), then delete the cursor+fallback recovery. See fvo spec §7.2.2 erratum and R5 §4.2.4 cross-refs.
notes: Linus PASS (2026-07-12, PR #262). Two non-blocking NITs recorded for posterity: (1) resolve.go ~407-409 retains stale pre-fvo comment prose describing the old cursor recovery narrative — candidate for a drive-by prose fix next time that region is touched; (2) ADR 0008 amendment claim 'no golden carries a Use outside branch 0' is vacuously true (no golden serializes Use records at all) — wording could be tightened. Neither affects correctness.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #262 (squash-merged 2026-07-12). Added Branch attribution axis to all three Use variants, stamped once at the addParameterUse emission chokepoint; resolver routes Uses directly via tables[u.Branch()] (range-checked to ErrOutOfR0Scope); deleted witnessInBranch/usePart/cursor+Part-drop recovery entirely. Both verified residuals pinned: unknown_property_union_sibling_branch.cypher (residual a, now invalid) and parameter_union_later_part.cypher (residual b, now valid, golden STRING NOT NULL). Spec closure in fvo §7.2.2/§7.2.1/§12, R5 §4.2.4, ADR 0008 dated amendment. Linus PASS; two non-blocking NITs in notes.

title: Semantic-scope attribution: WITH…WHERE aliased-shadow residual (post-fvo)
description: Follow-up from unfreeze cycle 2 (gqlc-fvo, PRs #116-#118). Part attribution on Use records is EMISSION-TIME, which diverges from Cypher's post-projection semantics in two documented shapes: (1) FINDING-9 (fvo spec §7.6.1): WITH-trailing WHERE PropertyUses mine PRE-swap (mineWhere at listener.go:283-284 runs before the Part swap at :292-293), so 'MATCH (a:Post) WITH a.title AS a WHERE a.x = $p RETURN a' attributes Ref{a,x} to Part 0 (a=Post) and the resolver ADMITS if Post has x, though Cypher evaluates the WHERE post-projection (a=STRING). No regression vs pre-fvo any-valid-witness, but not full Cypher semantics. (2) Intra-clause asymmetry (found in PR #117 review): a direct param in 'WITH n WHERE $x' lands Part 0 (pre-swap mineWhere) while an EXISTS-body param in the same syntactic WHERE lands Part 1 (natural walk post-swap, listener.go:627-638; parser pin 1712). Closing this needs a SEMANTIC-scope attribution axis (which scope evaluates the predicate), not the lexical Part axis — a distinct model decision, likely another ADR 0008 additive revision. See fvo spec §7.6.1/§9 and errata.

title: Model unfreeze: preserve same-Part second-reference facts on Binding (ADR 0008 additive) — R4 flow-typing Class B
description: Frozen-model gap Class B (R4 spec §7.5.3 item 2): mergeBinding (internal/query/cypher/pattern.go:373-401) DISCARDS the second occurrence of an already-bound variable, so a required bare-pattern re-reference of an OPTIONAL-introduced binding in the same Part (e.g. OPTIONAL MATCH (a)-[:R]->(b) MATCH (b) RETURN b) leaves no witness in part.Bindings — the demoter cannot see it. NOT closable by the Class A group axis: the witness itself is destroyed, not merely ungrouped. Proposal per spec §7.5.4 Axis 2, two candidate shapes: (a) RequiredReferences []ClauseRef or (b) ReferencedInRequiredBarePattern bool on Binding — additive, zero-value-safe, in-protocol under ADR 0008 post-freeze revision. PROTOCOL: model change lands in its own unfreeze PR (ADR 0008 revision), never rides a resolver-stage PR. No R4 fixture exercises this shape — the widening PR adds one. Independent of the Class A bead — owner may accept one, both, or neither. Owner decision pending.

title: Model unfreeze: OPTIONAL-clause-group axis on Binding (ADR 0008 additive) — R4 flow-typing Class A

title: On-disk procsig registry file format
description: Stage 14 defers the CLI-consumable on-disk format for procedure signatures. Today procsig.Registry is populated in-memory (godog step parses per-scenario declarations; real CLI callers would need to construct signatures from Go code). Design and implement a text format (YAML / JSON / .procsig) that mirrors the TCK's declaration syntax, plus a loader that constructs procsig.Registry from a file path. Follow-up to gqlc-im1.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #251. JSON on-disk registry format with strict-decoded loader (Load/Decode), canonical MarshalJSON, and Save round-trip helper. Format defensibly JSON — stdlib only, matches existing schema/query/validated precedent, extensible via omit-if-nil version field. Rejects bare null / null signatures explicitly (would otherwise silently produce the empty registry). Loader delegates semantic checks (unqualified name, duplicate column, unknown token) to existing NewRegistry so file surface and in-memory API stay lockstep. Follow-up gqlc-aqb filed for wiring into a real CLI.

title: Enrich CreateEffect to distinguish created vs pre-bound pattern variables
description: Stage 12 round-1 reviewer finding SF4: MATCH (n) CREATE (n) parses via mergeBinding, and CreateEffect.Variables comes out empty because the bindings slice doesn't grow (walk-order before..after delta is zero). Spec corrected to code truth (records only newly-created bindings). If a consumer ever needs 'which variables did this CREATE clause touch' including pre-bound ones (e.g. for typed-Create codegen over mixed MATCH+CREATE), CreateEffect needs a pre-merge variable list or a per-element created/reused axis. Blocked conceptually on a real consumer need — do not build speculatively.
notes: Re-parented from closed epic gqlc-33k to the resolver/codegen umbrella at the freeze (2026-07-03): explicitly consumer-driven (do not build speculatively) — pick up only when a consumer demonstrates the need. ADR 0008 names it a known deferred addition under the additive revision protocol.

title: Type params in EXISTS RegularQuery LIMIT/SKIP as clause-slot Uses
description: Stage 11 round-2 reviewer caveat (S5): a $param inside an EXISTS { RegularQuery-form } LIMIT or SKIP records the blanket ExprUse{TypeBool, ExprInPredicate} minted by EnterOC_ExistentialSubquery's parameter sweep, rather than the precise clause-slot Use (int, Limit/Skip). Recorded, not dropped — sound but imprecise. Cause: inner LIMIT/SKIP handlers early-return under subqueryDepth>0, so the subquery sweep is the only mining path. Fix direction: let the sweep classify params by enclosing slot, or narrowly re-enable slot handlers inside subqueries. Add spec §8 note when addressed.
notes:

description: Discovered 2026-07-02: core.hooksPath in .git/config pointed at the empty .git/hooks (absolute path), silently disabling the .githooks pre-commit/pre-push gates for an unknown period — every local commit/push since ran ungated; CI caught nothing because it is the authoritative gate, but the local budget-split design (README) was dead. title: Resolver: implicit grouping-key semantics for aggregate projections
description: Stage 3 (gqlc-npg) carries AggregateProjection with only its []Ref payload + the aggregate kind, deliberately NOT modelling implicit grouping (which non-aggregate RETURN columns form the group key). Per spec §9 (cypher-query-parser-stage-3.md) this is a resolver/Stage-4 concern entangled with WITH, and there is a real risk the []Ref-only payload proves insufficient and AggregateProjection must be reopened. This issue tracks adding grouping-key resolution once the model is frozen (gqlc-cta) and WITH lands (Stage 4, gqlc-v23).
notes: Linked to resolver stage R5 (gqlc-0mx.7) at the freeze (2026-07-03): grouping-key semantics are R5's scope; this bead carries the recorded contract (resolver-side re-parse; ContainsAggregate only as ADR-0008 escape hatch).
close_reason: Superseded by R5 spec B7 resolution (PR #101). The contract recorded here (resolver-side re-parse of ExprProjection text to detect nested aggregates) was retracted: the frozen model drops nested-aggregate structure at classification (classifyRichExpression returns plain ExprProjection; recovered text re-parses opaque, so re-parse cannot recover the aggregate bit). R5 landed the uniform-exclude posture instead: ExprProjection items are NEVER grouping keys; result-set effect is under-grouping when a Part mixes AggregateProjection with ExprProjection. Parser pin 'count in arithmetic' (parser_test.go:1319) is the explicit deferral lock. Escape hatch: Shape B ContainsAggregate model-unfreeze follow-up bead (parser-side bit set by classifyRichExpression during its own walk) filed for owner decision per ADR 0008 revision protocol.

title: Resolver: flow-type nullable bindings across clause structure
description:
Demote a binding's effective Nullable flag in the validated query when downstream clauses prove the binding must exist on every surviving row. Two regimes with different model dependencies:

(a) Edge-chain demotion (no new model structure beyond Stage 2 needed) — a non-nullable edge implies its endpoints exist, so chain 'non-nullable edge → non-nullable endpoints → demote those endpoints' nullability'. Handles the common case: OPTIONAL MATCH (a)-[:R]->(b) MATCH (b)-[:S]->(c) RETURN a, b, c — both a and b demote.

(b) Bare-pattern demotion (requires Stage 4 clause structure) — a required clause that reuses an OPTIONAL-introduced binding as a bare node/edge pattern filters NULL-rows. E.g. OPTIONAL MATCH (a)-[:R]->(b) MATCH (b) RETURN b. The model needs per-clause structure to record the second reference; Stage 4 (WITH/UNION) introduces that structure.

Per ADR 0006: the parser does not do this; the resolver does. (a) is shippable on its own after the freeze + resolver exists; (b) additionally waits on Stage 4.
notes: Linked to resolver stage R4 (gqlc-0mx.6) at the freeze (2026-07-03): flow-typing regimes a+b are R4's scope; this bead carries the ADR 0006 design context.
close_reason: Design captured and superseded by merged R4 spec (docs/specs/resolver-stage-r4.md, PR #98). Regime (a) shipped in R4 code (PR #99, 3b9d7f9). Regime (b) split per spec §7.4: cross-WITH → R5 (gqlc-0mx.7) admission-gate scope, no model change needed; same-Part → blocked on two independent frozen-model gaps (spec §7.5.3 Class A / Class B), tracked by the two unfreeze beads filed at R4 close-out. GH #21 stays open for the regime-(b) remainder. Forced past the open umbrella epic gqlc-0mx (open until R7 by design).

title: docs: Stage 1 spec §6 — make 5→3 arithmetic explicit (Metz cycle-5 non-blocking note)
description: In docs/specs/cypher-query-parser-stage-1.md §6 Layer-2 coverage gaps, the opening claim says ErrUnsupportedParameter is reachable by 5 fail-sites and the list shows 3 remaining uncovered. The intermediate isn't shown: 5 = 1 (cycle-introduced AUTHORED pin) + 1 (whole-map, corpus-covered by Match1[6] in mustReject) + 3 (uncovered). A reader counting 5-1=4 vs 3 bullets pauses unnecessarily. Insert one sentence between 'five distinct fail-sites' and 'the remaining three' that names Match1[6]'s coverage explicitly. Metz's exact suggested phrasing is in her cycle-5 diff review.

title: Stage 5 — undirected patterns
description: Support (a)-[r]-(b) patterns matching in either direction. Edge binding gains a direction-agnostic marker; resolution tries both orientations against the directed schema. May end up N/A if the schema stays directed-only — re-evaluate when reached. Per ADR 0004 §Stages.
