EdgeBinding gains a positive 'directed' marker (field+Directed() accessor+trailing constructor param+always-emitted JSON key); listener uses an inverted zero-value-safe 'undirected' raw field, polarity flip at toBinding. collectEdge stops rejecting left==right; directed edges canonicalise, undirected keep textual order (no flip; <--> guarded). godog read-core 371/179 -> 380/170 (+9 passed). Linus gate APPROVED. Branch stage-5-undirected pushed to origin (commits dae7fb3 prep, b474fbe model, d4fbedd unlock). Not N/A: parser is schema-agnostic, marker is load-bearing (undirected yields no single EdgeKey, resolver forms two candidate keys).

title: grammar: graphTypeLikeGraph and LIKE are declared under // 12.4 but belong to 12.6
description:
Found 2026-07-26 while building the gqlc-h9n.17 orphan detector, which derives a grammar name's owning corpus area from the ISO clause heading it is declared under in GQL.g4.

`graphTypeLikeGraph` and the `LIKE` token sit under the `// 12.4 <insert graph statement>` heading, apparently for typesetting reasons — they are semantically part of 12.6. Section 12.4 has no corpus directory, so the detector computes an owning-area set that no file can ever satisfy, and both names have to be carried as exemptions.

h9n.17 landed option (b): keep the declarations where they are and carry an exemption with a `why:` reason. That is correct and low-risk — moving declarations in a generated-adjacent grammar file to satisfy a test is the tail wagging the dog.

Option (a) is to move the two declarations under the 12.6 heading, which would delete two exemptions and make the ownership map exactly reflect semantics. Worth doing only if GQL.g4 is being edited in that region anyway. The risk is nonzero: the file is a community ANTLR adaptation (see gqlc-h9n.11) and reordering declarations can perturb ANTLR alternative ordering, which this project has already been bitten by — see the bd memory `antlr-alt-order-unreachable-alternatives`. Any move must be accompanied by a diff of the generated parser, not just a green test run.

P4: pure ergonomics, two exemption lines. Do not do it standalone.

title: schema/gql: mechanically derive the unreachable-alternative partition
description:
gqlc-h9n.2 pins 48 grammar alternatives that rule and token coverage provably cannot compel, and discharges `48 minus a checked-in exemption list`. Exemptions exist because some alternatives are not merely invisible but **unreachable** — ALL(*) hands every input that would take them to a lower-numbered sibling, so no valid GQL file can reach them. First confirmed member: `connectorUndirected#1`, stolen by `connectorPointingRight#1` (see gqlc-h9n.10 item 4).

The list is populated by hand today. linus proposed deriving it from `PredictionModeLLExactAmbigDetection` plus a `ReportAmbiguity` listener. team-lead **rejected that for gqlc-h9n.2 on soundness, not cost** (amendment A10), and the reasoning is the substance of this bead:

The mechanism does detect the case — the report fires under SLL with `exact=false` and under full LL with `exact=true`. But an AMBIG report establishes only *"these alternatives were ambiguous on THIS input at THIS position."* An exemption asserts *"EVERY input that would take alternative N is ambiguous with a lower-numbered alternative."* The gap between the two is input enumeration. A mechanism that resembles a proof of unreachability without being one is worse than a hand-list with a bead attached, because the next reader will trust it.

So this bead is not "wire up ReportAmbiguity". It is: is there a **sound** derivation, and is it worth having? Candidates worth evaluating before writing code — direct ATN reachability analysis over the generated serialised ATN (which is static and does not need input enumeration); grammar-level analysis with an external tool; or accepting that the hand-list plus its `stolenBy` witness is the right engineering answer and closing this as wont-fix with that reasoning recorded.

Note the current design already fails closed without any derivation: the exemption list is asserted bidirectionally against the actually-uncovered set, so an exemption that becomes covered turns the gate red and must be deleted. This bead buys confidence that the list is *complete*, not that it is *honest* — it is already honest.
acceptance_criteria:
A decision is recorded on whether a sound mechanical derivation of unreachability exists, with the ATN-reachability option evaluated explicitly rather than assumed impossible.
Closing this as wont-fix is an acceptable outcome provided the reasoning is written down, since the hand-list already fails closed.
If a derivation lands, it must not weaken the existing bidirectional exemption assertion, and must distinguish "unreachable" from "ambiguous on some input".

title: chore(lint): golangci-lint cache clean recipe or auto-clean for phantom deleted-worktree issues
description:
When a git worktree is deleted (e.g., \`../wt/gqlc-kww\`), golangci-lint's on-disk cache retains issues indexed by the deleted worktree path. Subsequent \`just lint\` invocations report phantom issues in nonexistent paths — 5 phantoms were observed during gqlc-71n implementation. Manual \`golangci-lint cache clean\` fixes it.

Options:
1. Add \`just lint-clean\` recipe that runs \`golangci-lint cache clean\` (simple, opt-in).
2. Detect stale cache entries in \`just lint\` and auto-clean when detected (harder — requires diffing cache index against existing worktrees).
3. Add a note to \`just doctor\` warning about stale cache when \`ls ../wt/\` shows deleted paths that appear in the cache.

Landmine flagged by linus during gqlc-71n review, 2026-07-18. Not blocking that PR.
close_reason: Subsumed by PR #396 and closed with gqlc-6rv. we8 proposed one of {a lint-clean recipe, auto-detect in lint, a doctor warning} — all three are reactions to a cache poisoned by a removed worktree. The per-worktree cache eliminates the poisoning source, so there is nothing left to detect, clean or warn about. Reviewer independently confirmed the subsumption is genuine rather than a convenient closure.

title: config spec §6.3: catalogue the explicitly-tagged garbage-int variant or hedge completeness
description: Residual from the Linus PASS on PR #266 (gqlc-8gp): 'version: !!int abc' reaches the typed decode and yields 'config: <src>: field "version": yaml: cannot decode !!str `abc` as a !!int' — the overflow row's wrapping but yaml's 'cannot decode' text, no 'unmarshal errors:' block and no line info. title: Release automation: DEFERRED (workflow-file guard blocks all in-workflow identities)
description:
## Repurposed 2026-07-18

Original scope (release-please, no binaries) has been superseded. See bead `gqlc-23e` for the full current design.

**Now**: automated release tagging + Go CLI binary artifacts on every release cut from master.

### Driver

- **tagpr** (Songmu/tagpr, v1.20.1) + **GoReleaser**, single-workflow pattern.
- No manifest JSON, no Node runtime, standard `GITHUB_TOKEN`. Rolling Release-PR UX identical to release-please.

### Why not release-please anymore?

Research (2026-07-18) surfaced three concrete blockers with the original 2025 plan:

- `google-github-actions/release-please-action` is archived. Live path is `googleapis/release-please-action@v5`.
- Seeding the release-please manifest at `0.0.0` is broken ([release-please#2087](https://github.com/googleapis/release-please/issues/2087)) — first `feat:` proposes `1.0.0`.
- `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot trigger required status checks on the Release PR — would need a GitHub App token dance.

tagpr sidesteps all three and matches this project's CI-speed priority.

### Scope

- **Semver**: `0.0.x` while experimental. VERSION file seeded at `0.0.0`; first release is `v0.0.1`.
- **Binaries**: linux + darwin, amd64 + arm64. Four tar.gz archives + SHA256SUMS per release. Windows deferred.
- **Homebrew tap**: deferred to a follow-up bead (`gqlc-1dq`) once the pipeline is proven stable.
- **Cadence**: `on: push: branches: [master]`. Never a required status check; cannot block merges. Feature PRs see zero release-related jobs.

### Acceptance

Squash-merging feature PRs updates a rolling Release PR (tagpr-managed). Merging the Release PR cuts a `v*` tag + GitHub Release with the four binaries + checksums. First release is `v0.0.1`. Manual tag pushes blocked by a tag ruleset. CODEOWNERS present.

_Full design, notes, and acceptance criteria live on bead `gqlc-23e`._
design:
1) .github/workflows/release.yml — on: push: branches: [master]. Single job. Steps:
   - actions/checkout@v4 with fetch-depth: 0
   - actions/setup-go@v5 (goreleaser needs a Go toolchain)
   - Songmu/tagpr@v1 → outputs.tag (opens/updates a Release PR; on merge of Release PR, creates the tag + GitHub Release)
   - goreleaser/goreleaser-action@v6 gated on `steps.tagpr.outputs.tag != ''`, args: release --clean

2) .tagpr config (repo-root .tagpr file):
   - version_file: VERSION
   - release_branch: master
   - major_labels: (none while pre-1.0)

3) VERSION seeded at 0.0.0 (tagpr convention; first bump becomes v0.0.1). Also read by cmd/gqlc version command via linker flags.

4) .goreleaser.yaml:
   - builds: cmd/gqlc, GOOS=[linux, darwin], GOARCH=[amd64, arm64], CGO_ENABLED=0
   - ldflags: -s -w -X main.version={{.Version}} -X main.commit={{.Commit}} -X main.date={{.Date}}
   - archives: tar.gz name_template = "{{ .ProjectName }}_{{ .Version }}_{{ .Os }}_{{ .Arch }}"
   - checksum: sha256 (SHA256SUMS file)
   - brews: block present but commented, referencing follow-up bead

5) .github/CODEOWNERS (from original 2026-07-01 design, still valid — last matching pattern wins):
   *                       @antranig-yeretzian
   /.github/               @antranig-yeretzian
   /.goreleaser.yaml       @antranig-yeretzian
   /.tagpr                 @antranig-yeretzian
   /VERSION                @antranig-yeretzian

6) Tag ruleset (GitHub UI, manual post-merge step) restricting tag creation to bots — prevents accidental manual v* tag pushes.

7) No just recipe: tagpr is GitHub-side automation, not a local check — nothing to run locally, so the CI-parity rule doesn't apply.
acceptance_criteria: Squash-merging feature PRs to master updates a rolling Release PR (tagpr-managed) with an incremented VERSION and CHANGELOG.md entry. Merging the Release PR creates a v* tag + GitHub Release with linux/darwin × amd64/arm64 tar.gz binaries + SHA256SUMS. Manual tag pushes blocked by tag ruleset. CODEOWNERS present. First release is v0.0.1. release.yml is push-triggered only — never a required status check, cannot block merges. cmd/gqlc version command reports the tagpr-injected VERSION at runtime.
notes:
Research (2026-07-18) driving the driver change from release-please to tagpr:

- release-please + GoReleaser remains valid (used by k8sgpt-ai/k8sgpt, cloudquery/cloudquery, lindell/multi-gitter). But three concrete problems with the 2025 design:
  * google-github-actions/release-please-action is now ARCHIVED. Live path is googleapis/release-please-action@v5 (v5.0.0 Node 24 bump 2026-04-22).
  * Seeding manifest at 0.0.0 is BROKEN (release-please#2087) — first feat: proposes 1.0.0. Would need to seed at 0.0.1 with bump-patch-for-minor-pre-major=true.
  * GITHUB_TOKEN cannot trigger required status checks on the Release PR (release-please-action#1179) — would need actions/create-github-app-token@v1.

- tagpr sidesteps all three: no manifest JSON, standard GITHUB_TOKEN works, no separate action-path/version bookkeeping. Same rolling Release-PR UX. Used by kazeburo/chocon, pyama86/pachanger, babarot/enhancd, ccusage/ccusage, youki-dev/youki.

- Binary storage cost: GitHub Releases are free and unmetered. Only cost is CI minutes (~3 min per release for 4-arch build + upload). Public repo → free.

- CODEOWNERS interaction: while solo, the catch-all makes explicit entries redundant; value is documenting intent for when maintainers arrive. tagpr's Release PR touches VERSION + CHANGELOG.md — once 'Require review from Code Owners' is enabled, owner must approve every Release PR (acceptable/desirable: releases become an explicit owner decision).

- Homebrew tap deferred: goreleaser has native brews: support; empty companion repo areqag/homebrew-gqlc + a HOMEBREW_TAP_GITHUB_TOKEN secret enables `brew tap areqag/gqlc && brew install gqlc`. Tracked in follow-up bead.

CORRECTION (2026-07-18, from Linus review): the description/design's claim that "Conventional-Commit PR titles drive bumps (feat: → patch, feat!: → minor)" is inaccurate for tagpr. tagpr bumps are LABEL-driven, not commit-message-driven — apply `tagpr:minor` or `tagpr:major` labels on the merged Release PR (or on the individual feature PR before it merges) to control the bump. Default is patch. Conventional Commits shape is still valuable for changelog readability, but does not automate the bump.

FOLLOW-UP RISK for gqlc-1dq: goreleaser v2 has moved the Homebrew key. The commented `brews:` stub in .goreleaser.yaml uses a key soft-deprecated in v2.10 and hard-deprecated in v2.16. When gqlc-1dq is picked up, run `goreleaser check` before uncommenting; expect to replace with the current key (verify against goreleaser docs at that time — the surface may have shifted again).
DEFERRED 2026-07-19 (PR #349): After ~20 hours of iteration, GitHub's workflow-file guard reproducibly blocks every documented mechanism for cutting release tags via GitHub Actions on this repo. All release-pipeline infrastructure has been deleted; bead stays OPEN as deferred/blocked. Users install via `go install github.com/areqag/gqlc/cmd/gqlc@latest`.

INVESTIGATION SUMMARY:

The workflow-file guard is a hidden GitHub behavior that blocks any token-based identity used inside a GitHub-hosted Actions runner from creating tag refs when any commit in the tag's history touches .github/workflows/**. Since every release-pipeline modification is inherently a workflow-file change, the guard triggers on every attempted tag cut.

Attempts and outcomes (all reproducibly reject with GH013 "Cannot create ref due to creations being restricted"):

  1. GitHub App via git push --tags — PRs #334, #336, #337 (tagpr scheme = release-please-alternative)
  2. Immutable-releases + goreleaser mode=replace — PR #338 (dead end: goreleaser cannot delete published-immutable)
  3. App with tagpr release=draft + goreleaser use_existing_draft — same PR #338 (draft-then-publish worked around immutability but tag creation still blocked)
  4. Fine-grained PAT (Contents/PRs/Issues R/W) — PR #340 → run 29670537576
  5. Fine-grained PAT + Workflows R/W — same secret rotated (Linus's non-blocking note said this might be the missing scope; empirically it was not)
  6. GitHub App via REST API POST /git/refs (bypassing git wire protocol) — PR #342, diagnostic step
  7. Classic PAT (`repo` + `workflow` scopes) — PR #345 → run 29672955808
  8. SSH deploy key with write access + webfactory/ssh-agent — PR #347 → run 29673254598

Community references consulted (all gave contradictory guidance):
  - github/community#116660 — "PAT is the only solution" (Apr 2024, referred to classic PATs)
  - github/community#109715 — App tag push fails on workflow-touching history
  - github/community#141159 — Fine-grained PAT with workflow scope still fails (2026, unresolved)
  - github/community#68419 — Deploy key + ruleset bypass (2022, pre-guard-tightening)

Empirical evidence that the guard is context-specific to GitHub-hosted runners:
  - My user identity from local dev machine via SSH keys: pushed test tags to same SHAs successfully
  - My user identity from local dev machine via HTTPS + gho_ OAuth token: pushed test tags successfully
  - My user identity from GitHub CLI: created tags via REST API successfully
  - Every in-workflow identity type (App, all PAT types, deploy key): failed with GH013

Hypothesis: GitHub tightened the workflow-file guard sometime in 2025-2026 to cover all in-workflow identities, including previously-bypassing deploy keys. This is not documented in official GitHub docs (verified 2026-07-19).

REVISIT TRIGGERS:
  - GitHub publishes documentation of this behavior with an official escape hatch
  - A new identity type or workflow-context switch appears that empirically bypasses
  - We accept manual tag pushes and shift the automation to trigger goreleaser on push:tags:v*
  - We migrate to self-hosted runners (speculative — unclear if the guard is IP-scoped or identity-scoped)

FOLLOW-UP TASKS:

  - Optional: uninstall gqlc-release-bot App from areqag/gqlc
  - Optional: delete gqlc-release-tagpr deploy key from repo settings

title: Parser: unary-minus over a projection (RETURN -n.num) accepts as a plain ref
description: Linus review of Stage 3 unlock flagged that RETURN -n.num parses as a RefProjection to n.num rather than residual ErrUnsupportedProjection. Cause: the shared precedence-tower collapse (shape.go nonArithmeticFromAddSub) reads OC_UnaryAddOrSubtractExpression(0) without rejecting a leading '-'. Pre-existing behaviour governing Stage 0-2 too, not introduced by Stage 3, and no TCK read-core scenario exercises it — hence non-blocking. Decide whether a unary sign is arithmetic that should be residual (value lives below the type-interface boundary either way, ADR 0005) and tighten the helper if so.
